title: No teachers in Houston: Abner Jones and the silent-movie trio
summary: Cobb calls himself self-made; the only man who could teach theory, Abner Jones, played in a silent-movie theatre trio and had no time to teach.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now, I'm gonna give you something else. Here in Houston, when I come up in the thirties, we didn't have no instructors. I'm a self made musician. We had one guy that knew theory and could teach it --but he was so busy, he didn't have the time. The whites wouldn't accept you as a black. Are you listening good?
Yeah. I know what you're saying.

All right. Abner Jones was his name, and we had a theatre here, this was during the silent movie days; it was a trio that played for the silent movies, and he was the drummer, and the xylophone player -- I didn't say vibraphone -- I said xylophone.
So it was piano, drums, and the other guy was a violin player. Anderson Lacy, And we'd look at the silent movies, and they'd play the prettiest music -- but they were good musicians.

Now that was the only man who could teach us any instrument, but he didn't have the time. Now, let me tell you what we learned from him. After I got with the Milton Larkin Loggins band, in 1936 is when I joined him. Milton Larkin.
